status: Source/version comparison plus failed ASR pilot; clock verification open; local/unpublished

findings.source_supported_observation: Documented official versions materially conflict on flight identification and notification times.
findings.source_locator: DOT release physical91/105/106; H03-P165–166/219/593; STAFF17 printed17–19
findings.contrary_or_limit: 2001 NORAD release/FAA table claim AA77 at09:24 and NA forUA93; 2003 testimony claims UA93 at09:16; 2004 account gives first UA93 notice10:07 and AA77 missing09:34. Reproductions and testimony compared; raw operational clock reconstruction not performed.
findings.hypothesis_bearing: See specific observation and counterevidence; absence of established attack intent is not an automatic zero weight for circumstantial evidence.

findings.source_supported_observation: DOT did not find evidence sufficient to conclude knowing falsehood on hijacking notifications; it also called the no-accurate-UA93-time explanation unreasonable.
findings.contrary_or_limit: OIG could not determine another motive, found no direct FAA–DOD chronology coordination, and retained human-error/memory alternatives. Neither blanket exoneration nor proven deliberate fabrication follows.
findings.hypothesis_bearing: See specific observation and counterevidence; absence of established attack intent is not an automatic zero weight for circumstantial evidence.

findings.source_supported_observation: The liaison/bridge QFR was known inaccurate by three FAA executives and remained uncorrected with the Commission.
findings.source_locator: DOT release physical84–85/87, reportprinted9–10/12; originalQFR reproducedphysical106
findings.contrary_or_limit: Retrospective accounts disagree about who would correct it. Knowing an inaccuracy and failing to act are reported findings; coordinated concealment or attack participation is not established. Recommendation to consider action is not proof of action taken.
findings.hypothesis_bearing: Affirmative evidence of knowledge plus noncorrection; relevant to a later-concealment/accountability inquiry. The particular reason and any connection to attack preparation remain unestablished.

findings.source_supported_observation: The AA77 website error was removed after OIG raised it in September/October2004.
findings.contrary_or_limit: This correction differs from the uncorrected liaison answer; no evidence cited here that the websites were posted with knowledge of falsity. Archived website editions not newly acquired.
findings.hypothesis_bearing: See specific observation and counterevidence; absence of established attack intent is not an automatic zero weight for circumstantial evidence.

findings.source_supported_observation: Mineta explicitly identified the aircraft as the one that hit the Pentagon, while admitting that he did not know the particular order and inferred shootdown.
findings.contrary_or_limit: The recollected exchange is affirmative testimony; its meaning is not a firsthand report of a stand-down instruction or verified shootdown order. Neither interpretation is proved by the quoted words alone.
findings.hypothesis_bearing: See specific observation and counterevidence; absence of established attack intent is not an automatic zero weight for circumstantial evidence.

findings.source_supported_observation: Mineta’s about09:20 arrival/five-or-six-minute interval conflicts with the Commission’s perhaps09:58 conference-room arrival and later inbound-aircraft exchanges.
findings.contrary_or_limit: The Commission acknowledges conflicting arrival evidence and absent documentary proof of an early authorization call. Raw PEOC logs and witness clocks unacquired. Do not pick a true time by authority or assume a later exchange is necessarily the same event.
findings.hypothesis_bearing: See specific observation and counterevidence; absence of established attack intent is not an automatic zero weight for circumstantial evidence.

findings.source_supported_observation: The published note supporting09:37 tunnel entry says the alarm data were no longer retrievable.
